{{Quote|Good afternoon, Kalend, Rycar, Kal, Elis, Nabrun, Az-Iban&hellip;thank you for coming. I trust the refreshments are adequate. I have some merchandise I need moved along the Sisar Run. It is quite an important cargo, so I've contacted each of you to make the run to ensure that at least some of it gets through. Your crew will be paid 5,000 credits for the run, with a 5,000 credit bonus if you are the first to deliver your final payload. Those who are interested, remain seated. Those who are not, please leave.|Mal Biron, offering a cargo to Nabrun Leids and a number of other smugglers|<ref name="SotSR ">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref>}}
The '''Morseerians''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] distinguished by four [[Limb/Legends|arms]] and [[Methane/Legends|methane]]-based respiration. Most of a Morseerian's body was covered in semitransparent skin that showed the underlying internal organs. The exception was the elongated head, which featured large, [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a small [[Nose/Legends|nose]], and a thin, triangle-shaped [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]]. When found on [[Planet/Legends|planets]] with an [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]-rich [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], Morseerians wore full [[Environment suit/Legends|environment suits]] and [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] that provided the methane they needed to survive. They usually flew [[Starship/Legends|ships]] that supported methane environments and employed crew members who could survive in such conditions.

Morseerians carefully guarded the identity and location of their [[Morseerian homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] from outsiders, and little was known about their history or culture except that they were a reserved and secretive people who had several colonies&mdash;including the world [[Morseer]], for which they were named. The Morseerians were clients of the [[Drackmarian]]s of [[Quelii sector/Legends|Quelii sector]]; after that species was defeated by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Morseer came under the dominion of the Empire. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Imperial investigations into the location of the species' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] drove many members of the species to secretly support the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. A few Morseerians gained fame in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large, including the fighter [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]&ndash;turned&ndash;[[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Did you hear that?''"<br />"''What?''"<br />"''There's someone in here!|Morseerian pirates in their Mos Espa base hear Anakin Skywalker in the next room|<ref name="TOT ">''[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Morseerian_AA.jpg|250px|upright|left|thumb|Morseerians wore environment suits and [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] to survive in methane-poor atmospheres.]]
Morseerians were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], bipedal [[Species/Legends|species]] whose bodies were essentially [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]].<ref name="UAA " /> With rare exceptions,<ref name="Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy">''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]'' shows a two-armed Morseerian.</ref> though, Morseerians had four [[Limb/Legends|arms]] where humanoids had two.<ref name="UAA " /> While the upper two limbs were similar or slightly larger in size to those of a comparable [[Human/Legends|Human]],<ref name="TOT " /> the lower pair, which extended from a second set of shoulders, were slightly smaller.<ref name="TSC" /> These extra arms made them adept climbers and multi-taskers and aided them while grappling in combat<ref name="UAA " /> or wielding multiple weapons.<ref name="TT" /> While all Morseerians had opposing thumbs, individuals had varying numbers of digits on their hands: some had five per hand,<ref name="UAA " /> others had four,<ref name="TT" /> while still others made do with three.<ref name="CSWE II 249">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', Vol. II, shows that Nabrun Leids has this arrangement. Nevertheless, the Hasbro action figure (see [[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]]) of the character features Leids with three fingers and a thumb on each hand. Darnada's Morseerian guard, featured in [[Darth Maul (2000) 2|''Star Wars: Darth Maul'' 2]], also has three-fingered hands.</ref>

Morseerians had oblong,<ref name="UAA " /> conical heads<ref name="CRC 3">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> covered in overlapping scales of [[Color/Legends|brown]],<ref name="TSC" /> gray,<ref name="UAA " /> white,<ref name="ANHSE 1" /> green,<ref name="SOTE" /> purple, or tan.<ref name="TT" /><ref name="head" /> The rest of their bodies were covered in greenish,<ref name="TOT " /> translucent skin that revealed the inner workings of their organs and the flow of their [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="UAA " /><ref name="AA ">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref> Their large, black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] lacked pupils and were located above a tiny [[Nose/Legends|nose]] and a triangular [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] slit.<ref name="UAA " /> Some members of the species had keen hearing.<ref name="TOT " /> Both [[Gender/Legends|males and females]] had slender builds similar to those of Humans in their early teens,<ref name="AA " /> although [[Breast/Legends|breasts]] distinguished adult females from males.<ref name="X-Wing Rogue Squadron 32">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 32|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 32]].</ref> Morseerians stood from 1.5 to 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="AA " /> They entered adolescence at age thirteen and adulthood at eighteen, and their life expectancy was eighty standard years.<ref name="UAA " />

In standard [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]], Morseerian biology required them to take special measures that made them look bizarre to strangers.<ref name="FF CAN5">{{FactFile|22|CAN 1-6|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}.</ref> Members of the species required [[Methane/Legends|methane]]-rich gas for respiration;<ref name="CVD ">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> exposure to an [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]-rich, methane-poor atmosphere suffocated a Morseerian in [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]]. Accordingly, those Morseerians encountered by outsiders almost always appeared in full [[Environment suit/Legends|environment suits]]. A typical example of this protective gear was form-fitting&mdash;although looser suits were also found<ref name="UAA " />&mdash;and included a complex [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''.</ref> It used an incorporated supply of methane<ref name="ItWoSW ">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> to create an atmosphere similar to that of the [[Morseerian homeworld/Legends|Morseerian home planet]]. Masks featured [[Goggles/Legends|goggles]] to protect the eyes and straps to attach to the head;<ref name="UAA " /> a side effect was that they made the wearer's voice sound mechanical, similar to a [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoder]].<ref name="TOT " /> The durable suits rarely needed repairs or replacement and were built with redundant air pockets and filtration systems so that they still offered protection in the event of a tear or a puncture. Although inconvenient, such suits provided additional protection against airborne [[Poison/Legends|toxins]].<ref name="UAA " /> On the other hand, they made their wearers vulnerable to fire, which could ignite the methane supply.<ref name="TOT " />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Nabrun_Leids_and_Kabe_Hasbro.jpg|thumb|right|Morseerians generally shied away from violence, but they were willing to defend themselves with weapons if necessary.]]
Morseerians were introverted, laconic, and secretive. They preferred to keep to themselves, talking to strangers only to obtain information from them. This loner nature prompted Morseerians to avoid confrontation, although they were more than willing to defend themselves if targeted by others.<ref name="UAA " />

The Morseerian obsession with secrecy was perhaps most pronounced with regard to the name and location of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="UAA " /> The planet was uncharted by any but the Morseerians themselves,<ref name="SWE ">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> although rumor placed it in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. A Morseerian would rather [[Death/Legends|die]] than give up the location of the world.<ref name="UAA " /> As a result, little was known about their native culture and customs. The Morseerians were at least nominally under the protection of the [[Drackmarian]] species. Although the details of the relationship were unclear to outsiders,<ref name="TaBSB ">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref> at least some Morseerians entered into individual contracts with Drackmarian overlords. Breaking such an agreement earned not only the enmity of the Drackmarian master but also a [[Bounty/Legends|price]] on the Morseerian's head.<ref name="SotSR " />

Morseerians spoke a [[Morseerian (language)|language of the same name]]. Many learned to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]<ref name="AA " /> or [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]],<ref name="TOT " /> although these were by no means universal skills.<ref name="UAA " /> Morseerians had two-part names. Examples included Chall Bekan,<ref name="CB CCG">{{CCG|set=Official Tournament Sealed Deck|cardname=Chall Bekan}}</ref> Myor Devker, Shalthan Leeru, Nabrun Leids, Bargeth Relb, Nilek Rillion, and Flyrl Sacorbel.<ref name="UAA " />

The species had access to galactic-standard technology and manufactured [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Morseerian craft were oval-shaped vessels that ranged in size from small [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]] to [[Bulk freighter/Legends|bulk freighters]]. Such ships provided their crew and passengers with a methane-rich atmosphere so that their occupants could move about freely with no need for environment suits.<ref name="UAA " />

==History==
{{Quote|What's that? A sick worrt?''"<br />"''Nah, dirty womp rat vermin.|Morseerian pirates, mistaking Anakin Skywalker for a womp rat|<ref name="TOT " />}}
[[File:ChallBekan-CCG.png|thumb|left|Although Morseerians tended to support the Alliance to Restore the Republic during the Galactic Civil War, Chall Bekan worked as an informant for the Empire on Tatooine.]]
The Morseerians evolved on a world known only to them, rumored to be somewhere in the Outer Rim. They lived on the fringes of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Galactic community|community]] for more than 12,000 years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. At some point, they learned the workings of hyperspace technology and spread from their homeworld, whose location they were able to protect from outsiders. They also perfected their own starship designs. Morseerians found a niche just on the edges of galactic society, many taking up employment as galactic [[Merchant/Legends|traders]]. At some point, they encountered merchants from the [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] species and established favorable trading status. The Morseerians founded colonies, the locations of which were not as closely guarded as that of their homeworld. The species came to be known as Morseerians after the colony world of [[Morseer]],<ref name="UAA " /> in the [[Morseer system/Legends|Morseer system]] of the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="EA ">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> They preferred environments conducive to their physiology; Morseer had a methane-rich atmosphere, for example, with vegetation beyond recognition to species only familiar with the [[Plant/Legends|flora]] of worlds with [[Nitrogen/Legends|nitrogen]]&ndash;oxygen atmospheres.<ref name="TaBSB " />

At some point, the Morseerians came into conflict with a fellow methane-breathing species, the Drackmarians. The [[Reptile/Legends|reptilians]] conquered the colony of Morseer,<ref name="AA " /> and the Morseerians became a client species under the protectorship of the Drackmarians<ref name="TaBSB " /> as part of the greater [[Quelii sector/Legends|Quelii sector]].<ref name="EAC ">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Drackmarians opposed the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] but were defeated and subjugated. Morseer was among the worlds claimed by the Empire as spoils of war, although the species officially remained clients of the Drackmarians.<ref name="TaBSB " /> The new government instigated an initiative to locate the Morseerian homeworld, and the four-armed species began to secretly report to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] on Imperial troop and fleet deployments. Nevertheless, few Morseerians openly supported the Rebellion,<ref name="UAA " /> and a few even aided the Empire instead.<ref name="CB CCG" /> In the end, the efforts of the Rebel sympathizers paid off, and the species' home system remained shrouded in secrecy.<ref name="AA " /> Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Morseer and the Quelii sector came under the control of the Imperial warlord [[Zsinj]], only to be annexed by the remnants of the Empire upon Zsinj's death. By [[137 ABY]], Morseer had fallen within a region of space controlled by [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]].<ref name="EA " />

==Morseerians in the galaxy==
[[File:Moorseerian.png|thumb|right|upright|Nabrun Leids left a career as a fighter pilot to smuggle in the Outer Rim.]]
Although far from common and rarely seen further [[Core Worlds/Legends|Coreward]] than the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], Morseerians were encountered on their colonies and at the fringes of society on other worlds. Morseerian [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] preferred ships of their own design or outdated freighters from other manufacturers that had been modified to provide a methane atmosphere.<ref name="UAA " /> Crews of such vessels tended to be other Morseerians or members of species comfortable in such conditions, such as [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]] and [[Gand/Legends|Gand]].<ref name="SotSR " />

Because many Morseerians in the greater galaxy took up trading, merchants were in many ways the public face of the species. They preferred to deal with partners with whom they had enjoyed good relations and a bit of luck in the past, particularly Squibs.<ref name="UAA " /> Morseerians were spotted in [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]] and [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] across the galaxy, including one in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="YCAC">''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''.</ref> [[Void Station]],<ref name="SWE 24">[[Empire 24|''Empire'' 24]]</ref> the [[Lazy Bergruutfa Cantina]] on [[Betha II]],<ref name="CS 65">{{JournalCite|8|Counterstrike (Adventure Journal)}}</ref> [[StarForge Station]],<ref name="FOP 117">{{WEGCite|book=The Far Orbit Project|story=Preparing for War}}</ref> the [[Power Dive]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]],<ref name="RR">''[[Rookies: Rendezvous]]''.</ref> and [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="THoTS">"[[The Hovel on Terk Street]]."</ref> At least a few Morseerians ventured into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] and joined the roving [[Ebruchi]] pirates, an adoption that involved them accepting Ebruchi culture as well.<ref name="TUR ">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

A Morseerian guard served the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] [[Darnada]] in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]]; like the rest of Darnada's entourage, the Morseerian was killed in a strike by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]].<ref name="Darth Maul 2000 2">[[Darth Maul (2000) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2000) 2]].</ref> A pair of [[Unidentified Morseerian pirates|Morseerian pirates]] had a base on Tatooine; when on the planet, they sometimes traded with the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] trader [[Watto/Legends|Watto]] for spare parts. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] had accumulated a large stash of hard [[Currency/Legends|currency]] in various denominations. While in the next room, they heard someone in the treasure chamber, but upon investigation it seemed like nothing more than a [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]]. Later, though, they heard the unmistakable sound of someone going through their treasure chest. There, they found a young Human boy&mdash;unbeknownst to them, a nine-year old [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] named [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was leading a group of escaped slave children to a rendezvous with [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] who would take them from the planet. The child attacked them with a [[Beamdrill/Legends|beamdrill]], the flame of which would have ignited the methane supplies in their suits. When the boy escaped with a portion of their loot into the sewers, the narrow entrance would not permit the Morseerians to follow him, and he got away.<ref name="TOT " /> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a [[Unidentified Morseerian orphan|Morseerian orphan]] was one of ten [[Youngling/Legends|younglings]] kidnapped from the planet [[Abregado-rae/Legends|Abregado-rae]] by the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] woman [[Kuvuta Pindi]] for transport to the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] criminal [[Dool Pundar]] on the planet [[Foless/Legends|Foless]], where they were to be sold into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. The Twi'lek conned the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nuru Kungurama]] and his partner, [[Gizman|Big Gizz]], to help her by claiming she was transporting the children to a placement center for the [[Republic Children's Aid]] organization. However, upon arrival at Foless, [[Foless Spaceport Authority]] alerted Kungurama and Giz to Pindi's scheme. The two rescued the Morseerian and the other orphans, who were then placed with families.<ref name="SA ">''[[The Clone Wars: Strange Allies]]''</ref>

Another Morseerian spacer of note was [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]]. Although more than qualified as a [[Pilot/Legends|fighter pilot]],<ref name="FF CAN5" /> he broke his contract with a Drackmarian [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] named [[Omogg]] who operated in the Quelii sector. Leids earned a bounty for his trouble and fled into the Outer Rim.<ref name="SotSR " /> There he traded a life of high-speed dogfights for one of smuggling. Leids flew a modified [[Ghtroc Industries/Legends|Ghtroc Industries]] [[720 light freighter/Legends|720 freighter]] called the [[Scarlet Vertha/Legends|''Scarlet Vertha'']]<ref name="CSWE II 249" /> and specialized in moving cargos between the [[Sisar Run/Legends|Sisar Run]] and the [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]] that led to Tatooine.<ref name="SotSR " /> For the right price, he offered his services to transport passengers anywhere they needed to go.<ref name="NL CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Nabrun Leids}}</ref> At some point, Leids began a partnership with the [[Bimm/Legends|Bimm]] smuggler [[Rycar Ryjerd/Legends|Rycar Ryjerd]]. Although the two eventually parted company and found themselves competing for the same cargos, they maintained a competitive camaraderie.<ref name="SotSR " /> In fact, Leids and Ryjerd were both present at the Mos Eisley Cantina in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] chartered the services of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] for transit to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Leids and his crew entered a smuggling race against Ryjerd and others. They took on a cargo from the [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] [[Mal Biron]] on the planet [[Sriluur/Legends|Sriluur]] with the understanding that the team who delivered their cargo first would win a larger and more profitable cargo later.<ref name="SotSR " />

[[Chall Bekan/Legends|Chall Bekan]] was another Morseerian who lived on Tatooine. During the Galactic Civil War, he became the leader of a cadre of non-Human informants. Bekan and his associates reported on the activities of both [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] and the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="CB CCG" />

{{Talesstart}}
Some time after the establishment of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], two Morseerians were present in a cantina patronized by smuggler Han Solo on an unidentified planet. The first was sitting at the bar, but the second burst into the cantina and seized a young Human who had been playing [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] with Solo. The [[Amara's son|boy]] was the son of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Amara (Human)|Amara]] and the Morseerian claimed that he would be taken hostage for the Black Sun criminal organization. Nevertheless, the Morseerian was killed when Solo shot him with his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] and freed the prisoner.<ref name="TT" />
{{Talesend}}

No known [[The Force/Legends|Force-using]] tradition existed among the Morseerians, although some were rumored to have been [[Force Adept|Force adepts]] capable of tapping into the energy field. No Morseerian was ever known to have become a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], nor were there any records of encounters between the species and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="UAA " /> Nevertheless, the fact that few outsiders ever saw a Morseerian without an environment suit meant that the presence of a Morseerian Jedi could not be ruled out.<ref name="AA " />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote| I'm intrigued by the Morseerians in particular. This four-armed, gas mask-wearing species is prominently featured in the ''A New Hope'' cantina scene (and has even been immortalized in plastic) but almost nothing about them has ever been revealed in spinoff material. (And now I missed my chance, dammit.)|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Dan Wallace Blog">{{Blog|danwallace|168|Endnotes for Star Wars: The Unknown Regions}}.</ref>}}
[[File:Morseerian_concept_sketch.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Concept art shows a Morseerian with two arms instead of four and with no gas mask.]]
The Morseerian species was designed as one of the background characters of the cantina scene of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]],<ref name="CRC 3" /> but the alien's true first appearance was in the second issue of [[Marvel Comics]]' adaptation of the film, published fifteen days prior to the film's release.<ref name="tcr">{{BookCite|title=[[Wikipedia:The Comic Reader|''The Comic Reader'']]|number=#143}}</ref> A production sketch shows that the species was at one point envisioned with no gas mask, pointed ears, and two double-jointed arms instead of four Human-like ones.<ref name="DB archive">{{DB|character|kitikkeedkak|Keed'kak, Kitik|oldversion=20020204035033}}</ref> Two Morseerian characters were created.<ref name="ANH" /> During production and principal photography in London, England, the four-armed aliens were known as the "Plutonians" or "Squid Heads," the latter nickname later being applied to [[Tessek/Legends|another squid-like alien]] during the filming of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. The four-armed alien's official name was slated to be "Quidultii."<ref name="CRC 3" /> One of the characters is visible in the film near the bar, while the other sits in a booth.<ref name="ANH" /> The Morseerian at the bar was played by a female extra.<ref name="CRC 3" />

In [[1995]], the game company [[Decipher]] established the character to be a male pilot named Nabrun Leids and a member of the newly dubbed Morseerian species.<ref name="CRC 3" /> ''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]'' by [[Kathy Tyers]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] in [[1996]] added a few new details about the species, such as the connection between the Morseerians and the Drackmarians. The species' background was more fully fleshed out in ''[[Alien Anthology]]'', a [[2001]] release by [[Steve Miller]] and [[Owen K.C. Stephens]]. Other appearances of the species have either been cameos (including the non-canon stories "[[The Emperor's Court]]" and "[[Smuggler's Blues]]") or recreations and flashbacks of the ''A New Hope'' cantina scene.<ref>[[Star Wars (1977) 2|''Star Wars'' (1977) 2]]; ''[[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope]]'', Part 1; ''[[Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition]]'', Part 1; [[Chewbacca (2000) 4|''Chewbacca'' (2000) 4]]; and the [[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale (webstrip)|''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'' webstrip]].</ref> In [[2010]], author [[Daniel Wallace]] included a reference to the Morseerians in the Wizards of the Coast book ''[[The Unknown Regions]]''. In his blog, Wallace revealed that this was because the Morseerians are an "Unknown Regions species." He also lamented not taking the opportunity to flesh the species out more fully in the book.<ref name="Dan Wallace Blog" />

Although Morseerian characters appeared in [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', the species was never presented in a format useful to players who wished to portray such characters. In the game's rules, Morseerians receive an extra action each turn due to their four arms.<ref name="SotSR " /> The [[Wizards of the Coast]] version of the game, the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', explicitly allows Morseerian characters. Such individuals have no appreciable differences from Humans except for their four limbs and dependency on methane.<ref name="UAA " /> Special rules govern Morseerians who wish to grapple foes in combat, as their four arms give them advantages over two-armed species.<ref name="HG ">''[[Hero's Guide]]''</ref>

[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine|''Episode I Adventures Game Book 8: Trouble on Tatooine'']] allows a player to take the role of one of the characters of [[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine|the novel version of the story]] as the children make their way through the sewers of Mos Espa. The player may choose to portray Anakin Skywalker or his friends, [[Arawynne]], [[Dorn/Legends|Dorn]], [[Kitster Chanchani Banai|Kitster Banai]], or [[Pala Kwi'teksa]]. The main sequence of events is identical to the novel version, although details may vary depending on whether the player succeeds or fails at various tasks. The choice of character also changes whom exactly the Morseerian pirates encounter. This article assumes that the novel version of the events is [[canon]]ical.

Morseerian-like characters appear in two issues of the Marvel ''Star Wars'' comic book, but neither is conclusively identified by species. [[:File:Possible Morseerian on Aduba-3.jpg|One of these]] is seen running from Han Solo and Chewbacca after a blaster fight on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]].<ref name="SW7">[[Star Wars (1977) 7|''Star Wars'' (1977) 7]]</ref> The second is the [[Unidentified individual ("Pig-face")|romantic partner]] of a woman Solo dubs "[[Pig-face]]," who gets into a bar fight with the smuggler on Aduba-3 to defend their girlfriend.<ref name="SW8">[[Star Wars (1977) 8|''Star Wars'' (1977) 8]]</ref>
